summary: This is a formal Technology Readiness Level (TRL) assessment document for "Dixit," a retrieval-based AI system developed by SpineDAO Foundation that answers questions over a consented congress lecture archive with passage-level citation and timestamp provenance. The system is assessed at TRL 6 (prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment), with TRL 7 contingent on completing a pilot with ~140 lectures in front of intended users. Key gaps include lack of measured operational usage, paying users, multi-archive retrieval, and live revenue payout.

content_blocks.title: Assessment Header & TRL Rating
content_blocks.content: Document: Dixit — Technology Readiness Level. Published by SpineDAO Foundation as a public lab document on 22 November 2026. Core assessment: Dixit is rated TRL 6 — defined as 'a system model or prototype demonstrated in an environment relevant to its intended use.' The document is a single-page self-assessment covering current capabilities, gaps, and the criterion for advancement to TRL 7.

content_blocks.title: Section 1 — What Is Demonstrated Today (TRL Evidence)
content_blocks.content:
Five demonstrated capabilities are listed:
1. Running deployment: The system is live and answering questions against a real congress lecture archive.
2. Retrieval with passage-level citation: Each answer names the specific passages it was built from.
3. Timestamp provenance: The cited second is read from the transcript (not generated by the model) and resolves to playback of the recording at that point — a verifiable, non-hallucinated reference.
4. Three-state behaviour: The system distinguishes and reports three distinct outcomes — an answer with citations, a retrieval miss, and a refusal — as separate states.
5. Complete withdrawal: A lecture removed from the corpus disappears from the index within minutes. Because the architecture is retrieval over an index (not training), withdrawal equals deletion rather than attempted unlearning.

content_blocks.title: Section 2 — What Is Not Yet Demonstrated (TRL Gaps)
content_blocks.content:
Four capability gaps are explicitly identified:
1. Usage at scale: No measured session volume against a full archive in front of intended users.
2. Paying users: The commercial model is specified but not yet tested against willingness to pay.
3. Multi-archive retrieval: The corpus is a single archive; retrieval across several societies' material with differing consent terms is untested.
4. Live payout: The attribution formula is computed but has not yet been run against revenue and settled to contributors.

content_blocks.title: Section 3 — Criterion for TRL 7
content_blocks.content: TRL 7 is defined as 'a prototype demonstrated in an operational environment.' The criterion for Dixit to reach TRL 7 is: completion of a pilot running a full consented archive of approximately 140 lectures in front of its intended users, with usage, conversion, and cost per answer measured over the period. The document states: 'That pilot is the next milestone. It is scoped, and the archive for it is consented.' This indicates the pilot is planned but not yet started.

content_blocks.title: Section 4 — Rationale for Not Rating Higher
content_blocks.content: The document explicitly justifies why the TRL is not rated above 6: 'The distance between TRL 6 and TRL 7 is the distance between a system that works and a system shown to work in the hands of the people it is for. Dixit has not yet crossed it, and stating otherwise would misrepresent what the next twelve months are for. An overstated readiness level is the first thing an experienced reader discounts, and it devalues every figure that follows it.' This implies the expected timeline to TRL 7 is within approximately 12 months from the document date (i.e., by ~November 2027).

content_blocks.title: Section 5 — Summary Table of Dimensions and State
content_blocks.content:
| Dimension    | State |
|--------------|-------|
| Architecture | Retrieval over a consented index. No training, no fine-tuning. |
| Citation     | Passage-level, with timestamps read from the transcript. |
| Deployment   | Live, single archive. |
| Users        | Demonstration only. No measured operational usage. |
| Readiness    | TRL 6. TRL 7 on completion of the pilot described in section 3. |

key_findings: Dixit is formally assessed at TRL 6: a prototype demonstrated in an environment relevant to its intended use, as of 22 November 2026.
The system is live and deployed against a real congress lecture archive, with passage-level citation and transcript-sourced timestamp provenance (non-hallucinated references).
Architecture is retrieval over a consented index — no model training or fine-tuning — enabling true content withdrawal (deletion from index) rather than attempted unlearning.
Three-state output behaviour (cited answer, retrieval miss, refusal) is implemented and distinguishable.
Key TRL gaps: no measured operational usage at scale, no paying users, no multi-archive retrieval, and no live revenue payout to contributors.
TRL 7 criterion is defined and scoped: a pilot with ~140 consented lectures in front of intended users, measuring usage, conversion, and cost per answer.
The archive for the TRL 7 pilot is already consented; the pilot is the next planned milestone.
The document implies a ~12-month horizon for the TRL 7 pilot ('what the next twelve months are for').
No quantitative performance metrics (e.g., retrieval accuracy, latency, answer quality scores) are provided in this document — it is a readiness assessment, not an experiment report.

milestones.title: TRL 7 Pilot — Operational Deployment with ~140 Lectures
milestones.description: A pilot running a full consented archive of approximately 140 lectures in front of intended users, with usage, conversion, and cost per answer measured over the period. Completion of this pilot is the criterion for reaching TRL 7.
